source._version_note: Retargeted 2026-10-22 to v3.1.1, the latest Tempo GA (2026-10-21). go.mod at v3.1.1 declares `go 1.27.3` (v3.0.3 said 1.26.5) with no toolchain directive, so the builder moved from the golang:1.26 line to golang:1.27.3-bookworm: under GOTOOLCHAIN=local and --network=none an older toolchain refuses the module and cannot download a newer one. Upstream's own v3.1.1 release binary reports go1.27.3. There is no go.work in the tree, so GOWORK=off is not needed (L-A50).
source._vendor_note: Tempo COMMITS its vendor/ directory (440 modules, vendor/modules.txt present), so -mod=vendor builds offline straight from the checkout. loki does not do this and needs `go mod vendor` first. Any dep_bump still requires a re-vendor, because the bumped module has to physically land in vendor/ or the build fails closed rather than silently using the old code. Sets source.vendor_committed so the vendor stage KEEPS upstream's own vendor/ (440 modules) instead of running `go mod tidy -e && go mod vendor` over it. The knob applies only while dep_bumps is empty -- bumps are stated as floors by `go mod edit -require` and need the following tidy to MVS-reconcile them, so the moment a bump is added the normal tidy+re-vendor path returns automatically.
source._submodule_note: ./tools is a SEPARATE go module (github.com/grafana/tempo/tools) holding chloggen and friends. It is developer tooling, is not imported by any cmd/, and must not be built or shipped -- this is NOT the etcd multi-module case, the product binaries all live in the root module.
source.source_date_epoch_provenance: the time release v3.1.1-CE-ubuntu24.04-r7 was cut (2026-11-20T08:50:06Z), by scripts/retarget.py --rev-bump: ReadyStack dates an image by when its release was packaged (owner 2026-11-10), recorded here once and used by every rebuild of the release; it builds upstream commit 9db7df79d2af, dated 2026-10-21T15:24:36Z (source.commit_epoch).

binaries_from_source.name: tempo
binaries_from_source._note: cmd/tempo/main.go declares package-level Version/Branch/Revision and its init() copies them into prometheus/common/version, which is what `tempo -version` prints -- so the -X targets are `main.*`, NOT a util/build package as in loki. Stamp the BARE version (@VERSION_BARE@) with no leading v (L: buildinfo.tag no-leading-v, from coder). Revision is the short sha of the tag's commit (@COMMIT:8@).

binaries_from_source.name: tempo-cli
binaries_from_source._note: The operator tool for inspecting blocks, the WAL and the local backend offline. Same module and therefore the same dependency set as tempo itself, so it adds no CVE surface -- every package it links is already in the image via the main binary. cmd/tempo-query (a Jaeger gRPC plugin, useless without Jaeger) and cmd/tempo-vulture (a load-test harness) are deliberately NOT built.
